scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is AITA (Ask if it's a thing) for not making their 7-year-old brother go to sleep. Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: The person is 18 and has a younger brother who's 7. The brother is sensitive to sleep, meaning if he doesn't get enough, he gets cranky the next day. The older brother was in charge because their mom wasn't home until 1 AM. He had a friend over, and everything was fine until the brother woke up and wanted to join them. The older brother told him to go back to bed, but the friend encouraged letting him stay. The brother ended up staying, watching the movie, and fell asleep on the couch. They carried him upstairs at midnight, and the next morning, he was cranky and didn't want to get up. The mom got mad, and the older brother is wondering if he should have forced his brother to go to bed. So, the question is: Is it AITA for not making the 7-year-old go to bed? Let me think about the factors involved here. The brother is 7, which is pretty young. He's sensitive to sleep, so missing out on it affects him. The older brother was in a situation where he had a friend over, and the friend was encouraging the younger brother to stay up. The older brother was concerned that if he tried to make his brother go to bed, it would lead to a tantrum, which would be embarrassing and exhausting, especially with a friend around. On one hand, the older brother is considering the immediate consequences of forcing his brother to go to bed. He knows that the brother might throw a fit, which could be difficult to handle, especially in front of a friend. He also knows that the brother can put himself to bed, so maybe he's trying to teach him responsibility by letting him stay up a bit later. On the other hand, the brother is only 7, and his sleep is crucial for his well-being. The older brother acknowledges that missing two hours of sleep isn't a big deal, but he also thinks the brother should learn about consequences. However, the mom got mad, which adds another layer of responsibility. I think it's important to consider the age of the child. At 7, kids are still developing their understanding of consequences, and while it's good to start teaching them, it's also important to balance that with their well-being. The older brother didn't force the brother to go to bed because he anticipated a tantrum, which is a valid concern. However, by letting him stay up, he might have set a precedent that could be harder to manage in the future. Another point is the role of the older brother. He's acting as a parent figure in this situation, which comes with responsibilities. Allowing the younger brother to stay up might have been a way to avoid conflict, but it also means the older brother is making a decision that affects the younger one's well-being. The mom's reaction is also a factor. She knows what happened and got mad, which suggests that she expects the older brother to enforce the bedtime rules. This could indicate that the older brother is expected to take on more responsibility, which he might not have fully considered. In terms of AITA, the question is whether the older brother's actions were appropriate. He didn't force his brother to go to bed, which led to the brother being cranky the next day. However, he also didn't want to deal with a tantrum and the embarrassment that might come with it. It's a tough spot because he's trying to balance his brother's well-being with managing the situation in a way that's less stressful for everyone involved. I think the key here is that while it's not ideal to let a 7-year-old stay up late, especially when they're sensitive to sleep, the older brother's reasoning isn't entirely wrong. He was trying to avoid a difficult situation and considered the immediate consequences. However, it's also important to think about the long-term effects. Teaching the brother about consequences is valid, but it should be done in a way that's age-appropriate and doesn't compromise his well-being. So, considering all these factors, I don't think the older brother is entirely AITA. He had valid reasons for not forcing his brother to go to bed, even though the outcome wasn't ideal. It's a tricky situation, and he made a decision based on the circumstances he was in.
